title: Point-valued counit pairings under coherent coefficient reconstruction
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $a:X\to s$ be separated of finite type [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and fix a compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Use the specified constructible exceptional adjunctions $P_n=Ra_{!,n}\dashv G_n=Ra_n^!$ and $P=Ra_!\dashv G=Ra^!$, with counits $\epsilon_n,\epsilon$, of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support].

Let $M_\bullet$ be a whole normalized quotient system [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower], with bounded constructible finite-Tor levels and common bounds and stratifications [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let
$$t_\bullet:M_\bullet\longrightarrow G_\bullet((A_n)_s)$$
be an actual morphism in the derived category of quotient-module systems, using the coherent finite exceptional system specified in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Assume all intermediate systems lie in that constructible finite-Tor domain. Put $M=R\lim\operatorname{Res}M_\bullet$ and let $t:M\to G(U_s)$ be its specified realization under the counit-preserving reconstruction comparisons, where $U_s=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$. Set $h_n=\epsilon_n\circ P_n(t_n)$ and $h=\epsilon\circ P(t)$.

The $h_n$ are the evaluations of a whole-system morphism $h_\bullet$, and its derived-limit realization is $h$ under the canonical compact-support and unit comparisons. After the point-fibre functor [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] this is an equality of coefficient-complex morphisms
$$\operatorname{Fib}_s(h):R\Gamma_c(X,M)\longrightarrow\mathcal O_E,$$
with $R\Gamma_c$ as in [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Rationalization and common-stage coefficient transport carry this very morphism to the counit pairings for the transported $t$ and $M$; these identities are independent of enlarging the finite coefficient field [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

If $c_\bullet:((A_n)_s)\to P_\bullet(M_\bullet)$ is a whole-system class with $h_\bullet c_\bullet=1$ as a system equation, its reconstructed class and its rational and common-stage images are sent to $1$ by these pairings. This last assertion is conditional on a supplied coherent class; it asserts no such class for an arbitrary $X$. No invertibility or smoothness assumption on $t_\bullet$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $N_\bullet=((A_n)_s)_n$, $\mathcal F=P_\bullet$ and $\mathcal E=G_\bullet$. Use the coherent finite adjunction realization, including its system counit $\epsilon_\bullet:\mathcal F\mathcal E\to1$, from [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. All its inputs are normalized with finite-Tor constructible levels by hypothesis. Define the actual system arrow $h_\bullet=\epsilon_{\bullet,N_\bullet}\circ\mathcal F(t_\bullet):\mathcal F M_\bullet\to N_\bullet$. Evaluation is a functor and the specified realization evaluates to the finite operations and counits, so $e_n(h_\bullet)=\epsilon_n\circ P_n(t_n)=h_n$. This construction takes the composite before evaluation and does not infer a system arrow from separately given finite arrows.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus] with $P=M_\bullet$, $N=N_\bullet$, $F=\mathcal F$, $G=\mathcal E$ and $a=t_\bullet$. Use its final, restricted-subcategory clause for the stipulated constructible finite-Tor domain; every object needed in the displayed composites lies there by the hypothesis on intermediate systems. It identifies the transpose of $\mathcal L_X(t_\bullet)$ with $\mathcal L_s(\epsilon_{\bullet,N_\bullet}\circ\mathcal F(t_\bullet))=\mathcal L_s(h_\bullet)$. The compact-support functor is $\mathcal L_s\mathcal F\mathcal R_X$ with its finite projections by [lem-coef-finite-adjunction-diagram-realization]. By [prop-coef-integral-exceptional-adjoint] the specified integral exceptional adjunction preserves those counits. Thus under the stipulated counit-preserving comparisons the transpose is precisely $\epsilon\circ P(t)=h$. In particular this is an identity of actual reconstructed morphisms, not a claim that equality can be tested on all reductions.

source.place: proof, counit clause: transported smooth trace and its coefficient-transported normalization; whole-system counit composites, point-fibre evaluation and preservation of a normalized class (returned Step 3)

proof.text: Apply the functor $\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] to the equality in Step 2. Its source is $\operatorname{Fib}_s(PM)=R\Gamma_c(X,M)$ by [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. The constant-value ring isomorphism $\Gamma(s,U_s)=\mathcal O_E$ in [lem-pod-integral-point-coefficient-adjunction] identifies its target with $\mathcal O_E$ concentrated in degree zero. Consequently the resulting arrow is exactly $\operatorname{Fib}_s(h):R\Gamma_c(X,M)\to\mathcal O_E$ with the asserted point-valued normalization; no interchange of point sections with an unconstructed limit is needed.

source.place: proof, counit clause: transported smooth trace and its coefficient-transported normalization; whole-system counit composites, point-fibre evaluation and preservation of a normalized class (returned Step 3)

proof.text: Let $Q_W$ be scalar localization to $E$. The comparisons of [lem-coef-rational-operations] identify the localized exceptional adjunction with the specified rational one and preserve its counit, also under finite scalar extension. Therefore, writing all source and target comparisons implicitly, functoriality gives $Q_s(h)=Q_s(\epsilon)\circ Q_s(Pt)=\epsilon_E\circ P_E(Q_Xt)$. This is the counit pairing for the transported arrow, including its map action. The rational point functor in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] is defined on arrows by applying sections and tensoring with $E$, so applying it gives precisely the scalar extension of the point-valued arrow in Step 3.

proof.text: For $E\subset F$, denote coefficient extension by $T$. The finite-extension counit compatibility of [lem-coef-rational-operations] gives, with the canonical operation comparisons inserted, $T_s(h_E)=T_s(\epsilon_E)\circ T_s(P_Et_E)=\epsilon_F\circ P_F(T_Xt_E)$. The natural sections comparison and its three-field composition equation in [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] identify the point-valued arrow with $\operatorname{Fib}_s(h_E)\otimes_E F$. By [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], morphisms and their compositions are represented over a common finite field, and equal representatives stay equal upon further extension. Hence the displayed equality defines the same morphism at the algebraically closed coefficient stage, independently of enlargement. The stagewise point functor of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] carries it to that same coefficient-complex pairing.

source.place: proof, counit clause: transported smooth trace and its coefficient-transported normalization; whole-system counit composites, point-fibre evaluation and preservation of a normalized class (returned Step 3)

proof.text: Suppose the additional whole-system class $c_\bullet$ is supplied. Apply $\mathcal L_s$ to the assumed equation: $\mathcal L_s(h_\bullet)\mathcal L_s(c_\bullet)=\mathcal L_s(1_{N_\bullet})=1_{\mathcal L_sN_\bullet}$. Conjugating by the same source and unit comparisons used in Step 2 cancels the inverse comparisons in the middle, giving $hc=1_{U_s}$. Apply the point functor and the constant-value unit identification from Step 3 to obtain $\operatorname{Fib}_s(h)\operatorname{Fib}_s(c)=1_{\mathcal O_E}$. Scalar localization and each common-stage functor preserve composition and identities, so the same equation holds for the classes and pairings in Steps 4–5. Equivalently the image of the coefficient unit under each class is sent back to $1$. This only applies functors to the supplied equation; it asserts neither existence of $c_\bullet$ nor invertibility of $t_\bullet$.
